Dear Doctor,

Re: Amina Ahmed, aged (8 years)

 I’m writing this letter with regard to Amina, an 8 year old daughter of Somali immigrants, who          Commented [t3]: Indentation is not wrong at the
presented with signs & symptoms consistent with meningococcal meningitis. Her condition                  beginning of the letter but it is preferable to omit it.

requires urgent admission to the Emergency Pediatrics Unit for further investigations & treatment.       Commented [t4]: eight-year-old

Kindly note that her father has good understanding of English.                                           Commented [t5]: and


 Initially, Amina presented to my clinic five days ago with fever, and lack of appetite, together with
a runny nose & a mild cough. On examination, she was febrile, (39.4), and her pulse was 85/min.          Commented [t6]: her temperature was
Her systemic examination was normal, with both rash & neck stiffness absent. However, despite
Despite the treatment & having some rest, her condition worsened over the next 3 days,                   Commented [t7]: three
complaining of continuous headache & lethargy. As a result, a urinary function report & full blood
count were ordered.

 On today’s review, the condition has regrettably deteriorated. Amina, after vomiting twice the
night prior, appeared listless & developed severe headaches. When examined, neck stiffness &             Commented [t8]: before
maculopapular rash over the legs were found, in addition to the lab results showing elevated
WBCs.

 In light of the above, my provisional diagnosis is meningococcal meningitis. A stat dose of IV
penicillin was administered and your urgent attention would be appreciated. All reports are
attached to this letter. Kindly note that her father has a good understanding of English.
Should there be any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,                                                                                         Commented [t9]: faithfully
Dr. Lucy Irving
Doctor
